title: Soccer Card Watch: The Beautiful Game is Having a Moment
summary: Soccer cards are booming, fueled by World Cup fever, rising superstars, record-breaking sales, and surging demand on Courtyard.
body_markdown:
Regardless of whether you watch soccer, you know exactly what Andrés Cantor sounds like:[“GOOOOOL!”](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HAKwmrtn1cw) It’s the iconic call that turns a routine strike into a ten-second fiesta—and while the sport it celebrates used to have a more niche following in the US, that’s quickly changing.


It’s safe to say that soccer is having a moment here in America, and as more fans tune into[the Premier League, Champions League, La Liga, and everything in-between](https://courtyard.io/blog/post/soccer-card-watch-new-signings-become-heroes) , The Hobby is taking notice.


[Soccer cards](https://courtyard.io/vending-machine?category=soccer) are one of the fastest-growing categories in the entire trading card collecting hobby right now, driven by a wave of young superstars, record-shattering auctions, and the success of the 2026 World Cup in cities across the country. Don’t believe us? We’ve got the xG to back it up.


Join us on the pitch as we go over the tactics behind soccer’s meteoric rise on Courtyard, from pack pulls to marketplace sales.


## **Why Are Soccer Cards Suddenly So Popular:**


The 2026[World Cup](http://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=World%20Cup&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ended in July, but it was announced all the way back in 2017. Since then, soccer fans had been waiting for the first North American World Cup since 1994, when the tournament toured the States. In-between 2017 and 2026, soccer broadcast deals exploded in the US, with companies like NBC/Peacock forking over $2.7 billion to broadcast the Premier League between 2022 and 2028—[and being rewarded for it](https://www.sportsbusinessjournal.com/Articles/2026/09/01/nbcs-premier-league-bet-pays-off-with-surging-us-audience/) with more and more viewers tuning in each week.


[Sports Collectors Daily](https://www.sportscollectorsdaily.com/soccer-market-growing-as-2026-world-cup-approaches/) has noted soccer’s upward trend for a while, too. Last summer, 24,000 soccer cards graded by PSA last July—as well as the 306% month-over-month increase in soccer cards graded by CGC last July.


While World Cup fever and increased interest in European leagues are one part of the increase in demand for soccer cards, the sport’s latest crop of young talent is certainly another.[As veteran hobby journalist Jeff Morris put it](https://www.sportscollectorsdaily.com/soccer-market-growing-as-2026-world-cup-approaches/) , “A sport does not sell cards. The stars of the sport do,” and between ageless talents like[Cristiano Ronaldo](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Cristiano%20Ronaldo&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) and teenage sensations like[Lamine Yamal](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Lamine%20Yamal&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) , there’s no shortage of stars for soccer collectors to chase.


## **The Numbers Behind the Boom:**


The 2026 World Cup began on June 11th, and the hype train hasn’t slowed down since. Once a not-so-distant last behind the North American big four sports (football, baseball, basketball, and hockey), soccer is beginning to creep up on the latter, even with hockey’s decades-long head start. Given[the 200-300% boom](https://athlonsports.com/collectibles/soccer-card-boom-2026-world-cup) soccer saw during the 2022 World Cup, it’s unsurprising that resale values are beginning to rise.


For example,[Card Ladder](https://www.cardladder.com/indexes/soccer) ’s soccer card index, which tracks the value of cards from the beautiful game’s biggest stars, shows an overall current value[nearly twice as high](https://www.cardladder.com/indexes/hockey) as[hockey](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BrefinementList%5D%5Bmetadata.Category%5D%5B0%5D=Hockey) —which rose 13% over the same time period as puck fans prepare for the NHL’s return in October.


## **Records Are Falling Left and Right:**


As soccer gains popularity in the world’s biggest sports card market, the next generation of global superstars is dominating the pitch, creating the perfect storm. Case and point:[Yamal’s 1/1 Black Kaboom rookie card](https://www.goal.com/en/lists/lamine-yamal-kaboom-rookie-card-record-auction-pele-lionel-messi/blt0b8c3833c01c2169) just sold for $707,600 at a Global Football Auction in July, blowing past[Pelé](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Pele&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ’s 1958 rookie card, which sold for $610,000, and[Messi](https://courtyard.io/marketplace?marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5Bquery%5D=Messi&marketplace_prod_recently_listed%5BsortBy%5D=marketplace_prod_price_high_to_low) ’s 1/1 Topps Chrome Sapphire, which sold for $317,200) at the very same auction.


“La Pulga” isn’t exactly hurting for headlines, either.[His Barcelona rookie card sold](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/46258113/lionel-messi-barcelona-rookie-card-sells-record-15m) for a record $1.5 million just under a year ago, making it the most expensive soccer card ever sold. And now that Messi has[retired from international soccer](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/49266819/lionel-messi-argentina-international-retirement-world-cup-copa-america) , the market for his Argentina cards likely won’t be going down any time soon.


…oh, and while we’ll stay out of the GOAT debate, Messi’s Barca rookie topped[Ronaldo’s green 1/1 2018 Panini Kaboom card](https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48863459/rare-cristiano-ronaldo-card-fetches-135m-private-sale) , which sold for a measly $1.35 million this May.


## **Hobby Influencers Are Taking Notice:**


From industry press and everyday collectors to influencers alike, the hobby isn’t going to miss the mark with the sport seemingly in the attacking third. Channels like[Blazey Collects](https://www.youtube.com/@BlazeyCollects) have built multi-episode series teaching collectors the basics of soccer cards, from licenses and sets to autographs, something soccer fans might have found missing from the web just a few years ago.
